Investigations (as indicated)

- Vitamin D: not recorded

- Other: emergency ECG to be performed by ambulance crew en route/on arrival  

Assessment & Plan (Integrating DDx)
- Acute central chest pressure with left-arm/shoulder radiation, diaphoresis, nausea, and dyspnoea in a 60-year-old man with hypertension, active smoking, overweight status, limited exercise, and positive family history of premature MI.  
- Most consistent with an acute coronary syndrome (myocardial infarction vs. unstable angina).  
- Other life-threatening considerations (per DDx): aortic dissection (medium likelihood), pulmonary embolism (low–medium).  
- Ambulance activated; clinician staying on call until EMS arrival.  
- EMS will obtain ECG and decide hospital destination and further management.  
- Aspirin allergy (mild swelling) communicated; need to weigh risk/benefit of aspirin administration in ACS despite allergy. No other medication allergies reported.  

Management Plan
- Immediate: EMS response, on-scene ECG, possible transport to cardiac center.  
- Advise patient to remain near open front door for EMS access; clinician to hand over details to paramedics.  
- Emphasize patient must inform all treating staff of aspirin allergy.  
- Further inpatient management to be determined by ECG and cardiac work-up.  

Consider:
- Pathology tests as above: consider troponin, FBC, renal panel, lipid profile once in hospital (not yet ordered)  
- EPC referral for allied health (10× visits/year): not recorded  
- Dental referral: not recorded  
- Optometry referral: not recorded  
- Audiometry referral: not recorded  
- Dietitian referral: consider post-event for weight and risk-factor modification  
- CTG registration (if not enrolled): not recorded  

Summary of Differential Diagnoses (from DDx):
- Acute coronary syndrome (myocardial infarction/unstable angina) – High likelihood: classic chest pain features, risk factors, ongoing symptoms.  
- Aortic dissection – Moderate likelihood: hypertensive smoker with acute chest pain; pain character less typical but must be excluded.  
- Pulmonary embolism – Low–Moderate likelihood: acute SOB and chest discomfort but pain not pleuritic and risk factors less compelling.

Quality checks
● Missing but clinically expected elements for pediatric assessment (e.g., growth percentiles, immunisation status, developmental screening, dental status): note pertains to adult; pediatric growth/imm-dev items inherently not applicable and therefore not recorded.  
● Internal conflicts between transcript and DDx: none identified.  
● Transcript quality (e.g., noisy/inaudible segments): clear audio; no major inaudible sections.
